summary.text: A 36-year-old woman with polycystic ovary syndrome, at 28 weeks of an in vitro fertilization twin pregnancy and without hypertensive disorders, presented to the emergency department with intermittent chest and epigastric pain radiating to the back, right hypochondrium and right shoulder, with nausea, vomiting and dyspnea. She was hemodynamically stable with normal vital signs. Initial tests showed mild thrombocytopenia and normal hemoglobin; acute coronary syndrome was excluded and pancreatitis and premature labor were considered.

Within ten hours of admission she developed a significant hemoglobin drop to 9.3 g/dL, tachycardia, hypotension, and worsening abdominal pain; laboratory tests showed elevated ALP, AST and ALT. Bedside ultrasound showed hepatic nodules compatible with hemangiomas and a small amount of free fluid. Emergency cesarean section confirmed intrauterine fetal demise of one twin and delivered the surviving twin. Laparotomy revealed right hepatic lobe rupture with a large bilobar capsular hematoma, treated with hepatic packing and drainage, and re-operation was planned for 48 hours later.

Postoperatively she required transfusion, coagulation factors, vasoactive drugs and fluid resuscitation for shock, with mechanical ventilation for respiratory failure. At second-look surgery the packs were removed without evidence of active bleeding; postoperative CT showed a large subcapsular hepatic hematoma. In the ICU she received antibiotics for suspected infectious complications, escalated after persistent fever, and had two hemodialysis sessions. On postoperative day 15 she developed pulmonary thromboembolism and started warfarin; MRI in the last weeks of hospitalization showed the hematoma and hemangiomas.

The authors describe the therapeutic approach as effective, with control of hepatic bleeding, and the patient was discharged after 42 days of hospitalization according to the case text (40 days in the abstract). The surviving newborn developed mild intracranial hemorrhage without need for drainage and needed 40 days in the neonatal ICU plus 4 days in the pediatric ward. After four months of follow-up, mother and child were in good clinical condition without recurrence or complications.
